issues.claim: R5-03 (§4.11 *The clock* (4) l. 8480-8484; V08 §3.6 (3) l. 1870-1875) applies a held late calamity's F5 targets' dossier events at the absorb that holds it — 'now at `W₀` as element events, finished (no Works)', each target's use closed and its building `ruined` (F5 l. 12205; l. 8588 'present as its ruin') — and lets the calamity strike at the first epoch a later absorb folds, whose `EpochInputs.dossier` carries no F5 record of it (V08 §3.6 (3): the F5 events ride the epoch only 'where `W₁` is after `W₀`'). V06 §3.11.1 (l. 2087-2090) defines 'struck in place' for the reverse order only: 'the hazards phase reads the epoch's dossier events for the F5 records tied to the calamity, and exempts those targets' uses from relocation … and the `dossier` phase's F5 then finds a building already struck, which is idempotent'. Nothing says what the held calamity's strike does to targets already ruined. As written the fire ignites at 'the building there' — the targets' centroid, a ruined target (§3.11.2 (1)) — spreads to any 'unburnt, unprotected neighbour', ruined targets included, and its `burn` sets 'existence → decayed with Works kind decay, stage CHARRED' (V06 §2.8 l. 720): a dossier ruin taken back to `decayed` with a new decay run at the later epoch, against §2.6 step 7's 'the level never falls while the building stays abandoned, decayed or ruined'. Another builder skips ruined buildings, igniting at the nearest live one: the targets never charred, a different struck set and `maxBuildings` count. Two builders, two behaviours on the path R5-03 defines (a calamity recorded in the week of the last sync); no bar runs it (T-V8-49 (g) and T76-1 assert only 'the calamity's strike at its first epoch's first week'; T-V6-27 runs on-time calamities).
issues.required_change: V06 §3.11.1, after '…which is idempotent.' add: 'A calamity held late (`DossierBinding.lateCalamities`; §4.11 *The clock* (4)) rides a later epoch whose dossier events hold no F5 record of it, its targets applied at the absorb that held it, ruined and finished (V08 §3.6 (3)): the hazards phase reads its targets from its `CalamityRef.targets`, places it at their centroid as any calamity, and strikes them by no op — each target building keeps `ruined` (its use already closed, never relocated, never taken back to `decayed`, no Works) while counting as struck: a fire's ignition is the target nearest the place and its spread starts from every target as a burning building, each counted toward `maxBuildings`; a flood's or a quake's struck set and count include them likewise; every other building is struck by the hazard's own rule, and its `deaths` reach that epoch's burial need (V06 §3.18.2).' V06 §3.21's hazards row (l. 3293) adds the input 'a held late calamity whose targets are already ruined' with the outcome 'its targets kept `ruined`, struck by no op, the hazard spreading from them (V06 §3.11.1)'. T-V6-27 adds 'and a calamity held late by a second absorb in the last epoch's own week (V08 T-V8-49 (g)'s case): at the later absorb's first epoch its targets stay `ruined` with no op on them, its fire spreads from them to their live neighbours, and its deaths are in that epoch's burial need'. END under V08: §3.6 (3)'s 'so V06's hazard phase strikes them in place' adds '(a held one's targets, applied at the absorb that held it, struck by no op, V06 §3.11.1)'; T-V8-49 (g)'s 'the calamity's strike at its first epoch's first week' adds ', its targets kept `ruined`'. (If the adjudicator rules the other order instead — a held calamity's F5 events held with it to ride its epoch's `EpochInputs.dossier` at that epoch's first week — §4.11 *The clock* (4), V08 §3.6 (3), §3.17's row and T-V8-49 (g) change in its place, and §5.3's coherence row names the held case, the dossier's ruined records then unmet on the map until that epoch.)

issues.claim: §2.7's support step (7) (l. 2623-2628, new this round, R5-02 (7)) 'keeps every station of the old deck — its key, position and support `ring` — and every span between two of them as it stands (`use`, `reason`, `state`, `held`)', then runs '(1)–(5) and the span rule … on the extension alone, from the old deck's last interior station (with none, from its other foot) to the deck's new end on the new ring'. So the old end span — from the last interior station to the ring-end foot, or a one-span deck's only span — is laid again, and it and every span beyond come out of the span rule with no `state` (standing): the old end span's `state` and its `held` `use` are not carried, nor (the kept list naming key, position and ring) a station's support `state`. V06 raises a fallen span only by `repairRaised` on a generated way 'whose reason is live again' (V06 §3.19.2 (5)), a declared way 'breaks only by a hazard or the landfall, and the user repairs it by hand' (§3.19.2 (1), item 101 R13), and `spans[].held` is 'an input override every regeneration keeps (§7.2)' (l. 2293-2294). An aqueduct sourced beyond the frame — the common ring-end foot (`RaisedFoot` l. 2312-2318) — whose end span its lapse, a topple or a landfall ruined before an epoch's rung crossing grows the frame has that arch stand again and a standing extension laid on a lapsed deck, with no repair, reason or event naming it; a user's held `use` on that span is re-ruled away. One builder follows (7) literally, another carries the end span's condition onto the extension (and keeps or resets a station's `state`): two behaviours, and no bar runs a frame growth over a fallen or held end span (T110-2's frame-growth clause and T-V4-65 run a standing aqueduct). VV34-r5-02 (V04, minor) notes the same re-laid end span for T-V4-63's vault wording only; one fix may close both.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (7): 'keeps every station of the old deck — its key, position and support `ring` —' → 'keeps every station of the old deck — its key, position, support `ring` and `state` —'; after '…its stations' keys minted after the largest the way has held ((5))' add '; the deck's condition at the old ring carries over: each span the extension lays takes the old end span's `state` (a `ruined` or `cleared` end span leaving each new span `ruined` or `cleared`, so only a repair raises it — V06 §3.19.2 (5)'s for a generated way, a hand Repair for a declared one, V06 §3.19.2 (1)) and, where that span's `use` was `held`, the same `use` held (an input override the extension keeps as a regeneration does, §7.2), its new supports standing (supports outlast spans, V06 §3.19.2 (3)); with no interior station, the one old span is that end span'. `RaisedFoot`'s comment '(the old deck's stations kept, the support step's (7))' and §4.11's frame batches 'the old deck's stations kept (§2.7's support step (7))' each read 'the old deck's stations kept and its end span's condition carried (§2.7's support step (7))'. END under V06: §3.19's lead '(§3.2 (9), the old deck's stations kept, §2.7's support step (7))' → '(§3.2 (9), the old deck's stations kept and its end span's condition carried, §2.7's support step (7))'. END under scope: T110-2's frame-growth clause, after 'every station of the old deck at its key, position and ring after the growth (§2.7's support step (7))', adds 'and, on the same aqueduct with its end span on the old ring `ruined` by its lapse and, on a second run, with that span's `use` held by a user's `setAttr`, every span the extension lays `ruined` and, on the second run, carrying the held `use` — no fallen arch standing again and no hold lost'.
